S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers shall report to the relevant regulator any thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, property damage, or emergency shut-down, within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a fuller initial investigation report within 10 calendar days. Manufacturers shall promptly notify affected customers when an incident indicates a safety risk or requires inspection, changed use, or corrective action, and in all cases within 5 calendar days of determining that such action is warranted.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A model with a failure rate above 5% shall trigger regulator notification, a corrective-action plan and retesting within 12 months. Until it meets the limit, the regulator may require risk controls, sales restrictions or other proportionate measures; exceedance does not by itself require automatic permanent market exclusion. Manufacturers shall submit per-model failure rates, sample sizes and test methods to the regulator and provide the results to customers who buy or are considering that model.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: All new units manufactured 18 months or more after this standard takes effect shall support remote emergency shut-off. For units already installed when the standard takes effect, manufacturers shall complete a technically feasible retrofit within 6 years; where retrofit is infeasible, they shall notify affected customers and the regulator, provide an alternative risk-control plan, and implement it promptly.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: All new units manufactured 36 months or more after this standard takes effect shall include built-in fire suppression meeting a regulator-approved performance and reliability protocol. Regulators may approve equivalent protective designs where they provide comparable fire-risk reduction.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A mandatory recall is triggered when a model’s annual thermal-incident rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 units of that model installed during the year. Manufacturers shall promptly notify affected customers of material newly identified safety risks and provide updates on corrective actions. The trigger requires effective corrective action and does not by itself constitute a permanent market ban.

document.section_notes: S2 has no sales stop and an open-ended transition, so a model failing above 5% (Hearth 10 at 6.2%) can keep selling indefinitely, with results given to customers but not published. S5 applies a mandatory recall at 8 per 100,000 per model with no transition, which captures Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9) but not Hearth 10 (6.4). S3's 18-month new-unit deadline and 6-year retrofit favour Northwind, while S4's 36-month suppression deadline sits at Halcyon's red line.
